```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../theme")
import bse_style, bse_anim
_ = bse_style.apply()

import html as _html
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
from matplotlib.patches import Circle, Ellipse, FancyArrowPatch, Rectangle
from scipy import stats
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

T_COL, C_COL = bse_style.ORANGE, bse_style.TEAL   # treated = orange, control = teal
PURPLE, GRAY, FADE = bse_style.PURPLE, "#9A9A9A", "#D9D9D9"
FENCE = "`" * 3   # a literal fence at line start would end a Quarto cell

def md_table(rows, header, align=None):
    align = align or ["l"] + ["r"] * (len(header) - 1)
    sep = {"l": ":---", "r": "---:", "c": ":---:"}
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "|".join(sep[a] for a in align) + "|"]
    out += ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in rows]
    print("\n" + "\n".join(out) + "\n")

def html_out(s):
    print(f"\n{FENCE}{{=html}}\n{s}\n{FENCE}\n")

def stata_win(txt, hl=(), bad=(), good=(), size="small", head="Results"):
    """Plain-text Stata output inside the Stata 'Results' window (theme/stata-results.css)."""
    body = ""
    for line in txt.strip("\n").split("\n"):
        e = _html.escape(line)
        for s_ in bad:
            e = e.replace(_html.escape(s_), f'<span class="bad">{_html.escape(s_)}</span>')
        for s_ in good:
            e = e.replace(_html.escape(s_), f'<span class="good">{_html.escape(s_)}</span>')
        if any(h in line for h in hl):
            body += f'<span class="hl-line">{e}</span>'      # block span: no newline after it
        else:
            body += e + "\n"
    return (f'<div class="app-window stata-results {size}"><div class="stata-pane-head">{head}</div>'
            f'<div class="stata-pane-body">{body.rstrip()}</div></div>')

def dots(ax, x, y, col, s=110, z=3, **kw):
    return ax.scatter(x, y, s=s, color=col, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.3, zorder=z, **kw)

def caption(ax, txt, loc="right"):
    x, ha = (0.99, "right") if loc == "right" else (0.01, "left")
    return ax.text(x, 0.97, txt, transform=ax.transAxes, ha=ha, va="top", fontsize=12.5, color=PURPLE,
                   zorder=10, bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.35", fc="white", ec=FADE, lw=0.8))

def beeswarm(v, base, step, width=0.012, sign=1):
    """y positions that stack points with close values (a simple 1-D beeswarm)."""
    order = np.argsort(v); y = np.empty(len(v)); placed = []
    for i in order:
        k = sum(1 for p in placed if abs(p - v[i]) < width)
        placed.append(v[i]); y[i] = base + sign * step * k
    return y

def logit_odds(p):
    return np.log(p / (1 - p))

SYM = dict(fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")   # ✓ ✗ ⇒ are missing from the slide serif font
PHAT = r"$\hat{p}$"                     # p-hat for matplotlib text (combining ̂ renders badly)
def anim_steps(s, items, height=470, fig_w=64, box=None):
    """Animated figure on the left + a numbered list of steps on the right.
    items = [(frame, html)]: the step appears together with that frame (frame 0 = visible from the start)."""
    w_in, h_in = s.fig.get_size_inches()
    height = int(min(height, 1180 * fig_w / 100 * h_in / w_in))   # keep the figure inside its column
    fig_html = s.html(height, first_index=0); plt.close(s.fig)
    lis = "".join(f'<li class="fragment" data-fragment-index="{fr - 1}">{txt}</li>' if fr else f"<li>{txt}</li>"
                  for fr, txt in items)
    steps = f'<ol class="anim-steps">{lis}</ol>'
    if box:                                               # orange "algorithm" box
        steps = f'<div class="algo-box"><div class="algo-title">{box}</div>{steps}</div>'
    html_out(f'<div class="anim-row"><div class="anim-fig" style="flex:0 0 {fig_w}%">{fig_html}</div>{steps}</div>')
```

2. **Matching on covariates** — nearest neighbour, exact matching

# 1 · Observational data {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## Did a job-training program raise earnings?

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
**National Supported Work (NSW):** a 1970s US program that gave disadvantaged workers (ex-offenders, ex-addicts, long-term unemployed) 9–18 months of subsidized work experience. We want its effect on **earnings in 1978**.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
nsw = pd.read_stata("nsw_cps.dta")
nsw[["age", "educ"]] = nsw[["age", "educ"]].astype(float)        # stored as int16: age**3 would overflow
obs0 = nsw[nsw["sample"] != 2].copy()                             # participants + CPS (no experimental controls)
obs0["u74"] = (obs0.re74 == 0).astype(int); obs0["u75"] = (obs0.re75 == 0).astype(int)
m1, m0 = obs0.re78[obs0.treat == 1].mean(), obs0.re78[obs0.treat == 0].mean()
tex = lambda x: f"{x:,.0f}".replace(",", "{,}")          # thousands comma without extra space in LaTeX
html_out(f"""
<div class="groups">
  <div class="grp t"><div class="n">185</div><div class="lab">Participants</div><div class="sub">D = 1 · mean 1978 earnings ${m1:,.0f}</div></div>
  <div class="grp cps"><div class="n">15,992</div><div class="lab">Non-participants</div><div class="sub">US adults from a survey (CPS) · ${m0:,.0f}</div></div>
</div>
""")
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment style="font-size:0.8em"}}
Naive comparison: $\\bar Y_1 - \\bar Y_0 = {tex(m1)} - {tex(m0)} = -{tex(m0 - m1)}$ dollars.
Did training really **cut** earnings by \\${m0 - m1:,.0f}? Or are participants and non-participants simply **different people**?
:::
""")
```

::: {.fragment .hyp-box}
This is **observational data**: nobody flipped a coin. People ended up in the program (or not) for reasons we don't control. First question, as in TA6: **do the two groups look alike before treatment?**
:::

---

## Was the treatment randomly assigned? A balance check

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}
For each pre-treatment covariate $X_k$: $\;H_0: E[X_k \mid D = 1] = E[X_k \mid D = 0]$, Welch $t$-test (as in TA6). If $D$ were random, we would reject only ~5% of the time.
:::


```{python}
#| output: asis
BAL0 = [("age", "Age"), ("educ", "Years of education"), ("black", "Black"), ("hisp", "Hispanic"),
        ("married", "Married"), ("nodegree", "No high-school degree"), ("re74", "Earnings 1974 ($)"),
        ("re75", "Earnings 1975 ($)"), ("u74", "Unemployed 1974"), ("u75", "Unemployed 1975")]
rows = ""; n_rej = 0
for v, lab in BAL0:
    a, b = obs0[v][obs0.treat == 1], obs0[v][obs0.treat == 0]
    pv = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False).pvalue
    n_rej += pv < 0.05
    fmt = (lambda x: f"{x:,.0f}") if v.startswith("re") else (lambda x: f"{x:.2f}")
    pcell = f'<td class="{"p-bad" if pv < 0.05 else "p-ok"}">{"< 0.001" if pv < 0.001 else f"{pv:.3f}"}</td>'
    rows += f"<tr><td>{lab}</td><td>{fmt(a.mean())}</td><td>{fmt(b.mean())}</td><td>{fmt(a.mean() - b.mean())}</td>{pcell}</tr>"
html_out(f"""
<table class="baltab">
<thead><tr><th>Covariate</th><th>Participants</th><th>Non-participants</th><th>Difference</th><th>p-value</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>{rows}</tbody></table>
""")
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment style="font-size:0.72em"}}
**{n_rej} of {len(BAL0)}** p-values are below 0.05 ⇒ the groups are **not** comparable: clear signs of **non-random** assignment.
Participants are younger, less educated, mostly Black, rarely married, and earned about 1/7 of what non-participants earned in 1974–75.
And these same variables also determine 1978 earnings ⇒ they are **confounders**.
:::
""")
```

## Without a coin flip, who gets treated is not random

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
In TA6 randomization made $\;E[Y \mid D = 1] - E[Y \mid D = 0] = \text{ATT}$. Without it:
:::

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.85em; margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\underbrace{E[Y \mid D = 1] - E[Y \mid D = 0]}_{\text{naive comparison}} \;=\; \underbrace{E[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid D = 1]}_{\text{ATT}} \;+\; \underbrace{E[Y(0) \mid D = 1] - E[Y(0) \mid D = 0]}_{\text{selection bias}}$$
:::
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
def node(ax, x, y, lab, col, fill=False, dashed=False, r=0.075, fs=21):
    ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), r, facecolor=col if fill else "white", edgecolor=col, lw=2.6,
                        ls=(0, (4, 3)) if dashed else "-", zorder=3))
    ax.text(x, y, lab, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs, fontstyle="italic", fontweight="bold",
            color="white" if fill else col, zorder=4)

def edge(ax, p, q, col, rad=0.0, dashed=False, lw=2.4, alpha=1.0, r=0.075, label=None, lpos=None):
    # shrink the arrow by the node radius, converted from data units to points
    fig = ax.figure; bb = ax.get_position()
    pts = fig.get_figwidth() * 72 * bb.width / np.diff(ax.get_xlim())[0]
    a = FancyArrowPatch(p, q, arrowstyle="-|>", mutation_scale=20, color=col, lw=lw, alpha=alpha,
                        ls=(0, (5, 3)) if dashed else "-", connectionstyle=f"arc3,rad={rad}",
                        shrinkA=r * pts + 3, shrinkB=r * pts + 3, zorder=2)
    ax.add_patch(a)
    if label:
        ax.text(*lpos, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=15, color=col, fontstyle="italic")
    return a

s = bse_anim.Steps("dag", figsize=(10.5, 3.1), margins=dict(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.99, bottom=0.01))
ax = s.ax; ax.set_xlim(0, 1.75); ax.set_ylim(0, 0.47); ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")
X_, D_, Y_ = (0.25, 0.17), (0.75, 0.17), (1.25, 0.17)
eXD = edge(ax, X_, D_, C_COL); eDY = edge(ax, D_, Y_, PURPLE, label="τ", lpos=(1.0, 0.21))
eXY = edge(ax, X_, Y_, C_COL, rad=-0.32)
node(ax, *X_, "X", C_COL); node(ax, *D_, "D", T_COL); node(ax, *Y_, "Y", PURPLE)
ax.text(X_[0], 0.04, "age, education,\npast earnings", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11.5, color="#555")
ax.text(D_[0], 0.04, "training", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11.5, color="#555")
ax.text(Y_[0], 0.04, "earnings", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11.5, color="#555")
cap = ax.text(1.42, 0.24, "X drives both\nwho is treated\nand the outcome", ha="left", va="center",
              fontsize=12.5, color=C_COL)
s.snap()
eXD.set_alpha(0.15); eXY.set_alpha(0.15)
node(ax, *X_, "X", C_COL, fill=True)
cap.set_text("compare units\nwith the SAME X:\nthe back door\nis closed"); cap.set_color(PURPLE)
s.snap()
s.show(height=225)
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.78em"}
**Idea of matching:** compare treated and untreated units **that look the same in $X$**. Within such a group, who got treated is "as good as random".
:::

---

## Two assumptions

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note title="1 · Conditional independence (CIA)" icon=false}
$$\big(Y(1), Y(0)\big) \perp\!\!\!\perp D \mid X$$

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}
Once we compare units with the same $X$, treatment is as good as random. **Untestable**: we must observe **every** confounder ("selection on observables").
:::
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note title="2 · Overlap (common support)" icon=false}
$$0 < P(D = 1 \mid X) < 1$$

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}
For every $X$ there are both treated **and** untreated units: someone to compare with. **Testable**: we look at the data.
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
For the ATT we only need to impute $E[Y(0) \mid D = 1]$:

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.85em; margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\text{ATT} \;=\; E[Y \mid D = 1] \;-\; E\big[\,\underbrace{E[Y \mid X, D = 0]}_{\text{untreated with the same } X} \;\big|\; D = 1\big]$$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.75em"}
❗ Matching is **not** a design like an RCT: it is only as good as the $X$'s you observe. It cannot fix confounding by **unobserved** variables.
:::

# 2 · Matching {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## Matching = imputing the missing counterfactual

::: {style="font-size:0.78em"}
A toy version of our question ($Y$ = earnings, thousand \$). For each **treated** unit, find the **untreated** unit with the most similar $X$ and use its $Y$ as the missing $Y_i(0)$.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
T_rows = [("A", 24, 10, 9.8, "1", 8.0), ("B", 31, 9, 7.1, "3", 6.0), ("C", 22, 12, 11.5, "4", 9.9), ("D", 28, 11, 8.4, "6", 7.0)]
C_rows = [("1", 25, 10, 8.0), ("2", 45, 16, 21.3), ("3", 30, 9, 6.0), ("4", 23, 12, 9.9), ("5", 52, 13, 17.5), ("6", 29, 11, 7.0)]
def swap(before, after, f):
    """'before' is shown until fragment f, then replaced by 'after' in the same spot."""
    return (f'<span class="stack"><span class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="{f}">{before}</span>'
            f'<span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="{f}">{after}</span></span>')
def show(x, f):
    return f'<span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="{f}">{x}</span>'
rows = ""
for u, a, e, y, m, y0 in T_rows:
    rows += (f'<tr><td class="unit-t">{u}</td><td>1</td><td>{a}</td><td>{e}</td><td><b>{y:.1f}</b></td>'
             f'<td>{swap("<span class=miss>?</span>", f"<span class=fill>{y0:.1f}</span>", 1)}</td>'
             f'<td>{show(f"<span class=fill>#{m}</span>", 1)}</td>'
             f'<td>{show(f"<span class=tau>{y - y0:+.1f}</span>", 2)}</td></tr>')
for k, (u, a, e, y) in enumerate(C_rows):
    sep = ' class="sep"' if k == 0 else ""
    rows += (f'<tr{sep}><td class="unit-c">#{u}</td><td>0</td><td>{a}</td><td>{e}</td>'
             f'<td><span class=miss>?</span></td><td><b>{y:.1f}</b></td><td></td><td></td></tr>')
att = np.mean([y - y0 for *_, y, m, y0 in T_rows])
naive = np.mean([r[3] for r in T_rows]) - np.mean([r[3] for r in C_rows])
html_out(f"""
<table class="impute">
<thead><tr><th>Unit</th><th>D</th><th>Age</th><th>Educ.</th><th>Y(1)</th><th>Y(0)</th><th>Matched to</th><th>τ̂ᵢ = Y(1) − Y(0)</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>{rows}</tbody></table>
""")
print(f"""

::: {{.fragment fragment-index=3}}
$$\\widehat{{\\text{{ATT}}}} = \\frac{{1}}{{N_1}}\\sum_{{i:\\,D_i = 1}} \\big(Y_i - Y_{{j(i)}}\\big) = \\mathbf{{{att:+.2f}}}$$
:::

::: {{.fragment fragment-index=4}}
Naive: $\\bar Y_1 - \\bar Y_0 = {np.mean([r[3] for r in T_rows]):.2f} - {np.mean([r[3] for r in C_rows]):.2f} = \\mathbf{{{naive:+.2f}}}$, because the untreated #2 and #5 are older and more educated: not comparable.
:::

""")
```

## Building intuition: two covariates

```{python}
#| output: asis
rngA = np.random.default_rng(12)
nT, nC = 12, 45
toyA = pd.DataFrame({
    "educ": np.r_[rngA.normal(10.5, 1.5, nT), rngA.normal(13.2, 2.4, nC)].clip(7.6, 19.4),
    "age":  np.r_[rngA.normal(29, 5.5, nT), rngA.normal(41, 10, nC)].clip(19, 64),
    "D":    np.r_[np.ones(nT, int), np.zeros(nC, int)]})
XA = toyA[["educ", "age"]].values
covA = np.cov(XA.T); VI = np.linalg.inv(covA)
tA, cA = np.where(toyA.D == 1)[0], np.where(toyA.D == 0)[0]
DA = cdist(XA[tA], XA[cA], "mahalanobis", VI=VI)
pairsA, usedA, doneA = [], set(), set()
for flat in np.argsort(DA, axis=None):                     # greedy: closest available pair first, no replacement
    i, j = np.unravel_index(flat, DA.shape)
    if i in doneA or j in usedA: continue
    doneA.add(i); usedA.add(j); pairsA.append((tA[i], cA[j]))
pairsA.sort(key=lambda pr: pr[0])
matchedC = np.array([c for _, c in pairsA])

XL, YL = (7, 20), (17, 66)
xs, ys = np.linspace(*XL, 200), np.linspace(*YL, 200)

def setup_nn(name):
    s = bse_anim.Steps(name, figsize=(8.6, 5.2), margins=dict(left=0.1, right=0.80, top=0.80, bottom=0.12))
    ax = s.ax
    axT = s.fig.add_axes([0.1, 0.81, 0.70, 0.14]); axR = s.fig.add_axes([0.805, 0.12, 0.13, 0.68])
    for a in (axT, axR): a.axis("off")
    axT.set_xlim(*XL); axR.set_ylim(*YL)
    ax.set_xlim(*XL); ax.set_ylim(*YL); ax.set_xlabel("Education (years)"); ax.set_ylabel("Age")
    return s, ax, axT, axR

def draw_marg(axT, axR, idxT, idxC):
    arts = []; mx = my = 0
    for idx, col in ((idxT, T_COL), (idxC, C_COL)):
        kx = stats.gaussian_kde(toyA.educ.values[idx])(xs); ky = stats.gaussian_kde(toyA.age.values[idx])(ys)
        arts += [axT.fill_between(xs, kx, color=col, alpha=0.3, lw=0)] + axT.plot(xs, kx, color=col, lw=1.8)
        arts += [axR.fill_betweenx(ys, ky, color=col, alpha=0.3, lw=0)] + axR.plot(ky, ys, color=col, lw=1.8)
        mx, my = max(mx, kx.max()), max(my, ky.max())
    axT.set_ylim(0, mx * 1.05); axR.set_xlim(0, my * 1.05)
    return arts

s, ax, axT, axR = setup_nn("twocov")
dots(ax, toyA.educ[cA], toyA.age[cA], C_COL, label="Untreated (D = 0)")
dots(ax, toyA.educ[tA], toyA.age[tA], T_COL, label="Treated (D = 1)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=11.5, frameon=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor=FADE)
s.snap()
draw_marg(axT, axR, tA, cA)
s.snap()
ax.axvline(toyA.educ[tA].mean(), color=T_COL, ls=":", lw=1.6); ax.axvline(toyA.educ[cA].mean(), color=C_COL, ls=":", lw=1.6)
ax.axhline(toyA.age[tA].mean(), color=T_COL, ls=":", lw=1.6); ax.axhline(toyA.age[cA].mean(), color=C_COL, ls=":", lw=1.6)
s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, "Two covariates, education and age: each dot is one person."),
    (1, "Their distributions (top: education, right: age) <b>differ</b>: treated are younger and less educated."),
    (2, "So do the means (dotted lines). Comparing all of them is comparing apples and oranges."),
], height=520, fig_w=64)
```

## Nearest-neighbour matching

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}
Distance between treated $i$ and untreated $j$ (Mahalanobis, scale-free): $\;d(i,j) = \sqrt{(X_i - X_j)'\,S^{-1}\,(X_i - X_j)}$, with $S$ the covariance matrix of $X$.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
s, ax, axT, axR = setup_nn("nn")
scC = dots(ax, toyA.educ[cA], toyA.age[cA], C_COL)
dots(ax, toyA.educ[tA], toyA.age[tA], T_COL)
marg = draw_marg(axT, axR, tA, cA)
s.snap()
# 2) one treated unit: distance contours are ellipses
i0, j0 = pairsA[0]
ev, evec = np.linalg.eigh(covA); ang = np.degrees(np.arctan2(evec[1, 1], evec[0, 1]))
ells = []
for r_, a_ in ((0.5, 0.9), (1.0, 0.6), (1.5, 0.35)):
    e = Ellipse(XA[i0], 2 * r_ * np.sqrt(ev[1]), 2 * r_ * np.sqrt(ev[0]), angle=ang, fill=False,
                ec=PURPLE, lw=1.5, ls="--", alpha=a_, zorder=2)
    ax.add_patch(e); ells.append(e)
hl = ax.scatter(*XA[i0], s=320, facecolor="none", edgecolor=PURPLE, lw=2.4, zorder=4)
arr = ax.annotate("", xy=XA[j0], xytext=XA[i0], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=PURPLE, lw=2.2, mutation_scale=16), zorder=5)
s.snap()
# 3) all matches
for e in ells: e.remove()
hl.remove(); arr.remove()
for i, j in pairsA:
    ax.plot(*zip(XA[i], XA[j]), color=PURPLE, lw=1.6, alpha=0.75, zorder=2)
s.snap()
# 4) drop unmatched controls, re-draw the marginals
cols = np.array([C_COL if j in set(matchedC) else FADE for j in cA])
scC.set_facecolor(cols); scC.set_edgecolor(["white" if c == C_COL else FADE for c in cols])
for a in marg: a.remove()
draw_marg(axT, axR, tA, matchedC)
s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, "Start from all treated and untreated units."),
    (1, "Take one treated unit and find its <b>nearest</b> untreated neighbour (dashed ellipses: points at the same distance)."),
    (2, "Repeat for every treated unit: closest pairs first, each untreated used once (no replacement)."),
    (3, "Drop the untreated units that were not used: the matched groups now <b>look alike</b> (top and right)."),
], height=520, fig_w=62, box="Nearest-neighbour matching")
```

## Choices you have to make

```{python}
#| output: asis
s = bse_anim.Steps("choices", figsize=(11.4, 3.5), ncols=3,
                   margins=dict(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.86, bottom=0.03, wspace=0.08))
for a in s.ax:
    a.set_xlim(0, 1); a.set_ylim(0, 1); a.set_aspect("equal"); a.set_xticks([]); a.set_yticks([])
    for sp in a.spines.values(): sp.set_visible(True); sp.set_color(FADE)
    a.grid(False)
a1, a2, a3 = s.ax
def link(a, p, q, **kw):
    a.plot(*zip(p, q), color=kw.pop("color", PURPLE), lw=kw.pop("lw", 2), zorder=2, **kw)
# (a) caliper
a1.set_title("Caliper: a maximum distance", fontsize=14)
t1, c1, t2, c2 = (0.28, 0.62), (0.40, 0.52), (0.70, 0.30), (0.90, 0.80)
for t in (t1, t2): a1.add_patch(Circle(t, 0.17, fc=PURPLE, alpha=0.07, ec=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.4))
link(a1, t1, c1); link(a1, t2, c2, ls=":", color=GRAY)
a1.scatter([0.80], [0.55], marker="x", s=160, color="#C0392B", lw=3, zorder=4)
a1.text(0.5, 0.04, "no control within the caliper\n→ treated unit dropped", ha="center", fontsize=11, color="#C0392B")
dots(a1, *zip(c1, c2), C_COL, s=150); dots(a1, *zip(t1, t2), T_COL, s=150)
# (b) replacement
a2.set_title("With replacement", fontsize=14)
ts, c_ = [(0.30, 0.68), (0.66, 0.70)], (0.48, 0.45)
for t in ts: link(a2, t, c_)
dots(a2, [0.15, 0.85], [0.15, 0.2], C_COL, s=150); dots(a2, [c_[0]], [c_[1]], C_COL, s=150)
dots(a2, *zip(*ts), T_COL, s=150)
a2.text(0.5, 0.08, "the best control is used twice", ha="center", fontsize=11, color=PURPLE)
# (c) k neighbours
a3.set_title("k = 3 neighbours", fontsize=14)
t_, cs = (0.5, 0.58), [(0.30, 0.40), (0.55, 0.30), (0.75, 0.50)]
for c in cs:
    link(a3, t_, c); a3.text((t_[0] + c[0]) / 2 + 0.04, (t_[1] + c[1]) / 2, "⅓", fontsize=13, color=PURPLE)
dots(a3, *zip(*cs), C_COL, s=150); dots(a3, [t_[0]], [t_[1]], T_COL, s=150)
a3.text(0.5, 0.08, r"$\hat{Y}_i(0)$ = average of 3 controls", ha="center", fontsize=11, color=PURPLE)
a2.set_visible(False); a3.set_visible(False); s.snap()
a2.set_visible(True); s.snap()
a3.set_visible(True); s.snap()
s.show(height=300)
```

::: {.fragment .tight style="font-size:0.7em"}
| Choice | Bias | Variance |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| Tighter caliper | ↓ (closer matches) | ↑ (fewer treated kept) — and the estimand changes! |
| With replacement | ↓ (always the closest control) | ↑ (few controls used many times) |
| More neighbours $k$ | ↑ (the 3rd closest is worse) | ↓ (average of more controls) |
:::

## Exact matching

```{python}
#| output: asis
rngB = np.random.default_rng(5)
nB = 160
toyB = pd.DataFrame({"educ": rngB.normal(13, 2.6, nB).clip(7.5, 19.5), "age": rngB.normal(40, 11, nB).clip(18, 66)})
toyB["D"] = rngB.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(-0.8 - 0.55 * (toyB.educ - 13) - 0.07 * (toyB.age - 40)))))
ex, ey = np.linspace(7.5, 19.5, 7), np.linspace(18, 66, 7)
toyB["cell"] = list(zip(np.clip(np.digitize(toyB.educ, ex) - 1, 0, 5), np.clip(np.digitize(toyB.age, ey) - 1, 0, 5)))
cell_has = toyB.groupby("cell").D.agg(["min", "max"])
both = set(cell_has.index[(cell_has["min"] == 0) & (cell_has["max"] == 1)])
onlyT = set(cell_has.index[(cell_has["min"] == 1)])
nT_un = int(((toyB.D == 1) & toyB.cell.isin(onlyT)).sum()); nT_all = int(toyB.D.sum())

s = bse_anim.Steps("exact", figsize=(8.2, 5.0), margins=dict(left=0.1, right=0.97, top=0.96, bottom=0.12))
ax = s.ax

dots(ax, toyB.educ[toyB.D == 0], toyB.age[toyB.D == 0], C_COL, s=60, label="Untreated")
dots(ax, toyB.educ[toyB.D == 1], toyB.age[toyB.D == 1], T_COL, s=60, label="Treated")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=11, frameon=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor=FADE)

for v in ex: ax.axvline(v, color="#888", lw=1)
for v in ey: ax.axhline(v, color="#888", lw=1)
s.snap()
for (i, j) in both | onlyT:
    fc = "#CDEBEE" if (i, j) in both else "#FBD9B8"
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((ex[i], ey[j]), ex[1] - ex[0], ey[1] - ey[0], fc=fc, ec="none", zorder=0))
s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, "Compare a treated unit only with untreated units that have <b>exactly the same X</b>."),
    (1, "With continuous X, first make groups: 6 education × 6 age groups = <b>36 cells</b>. Same cell = same X."),
    (2, f'<span class="cellbox teal"></span> treated <b>and</b> untreated in the cell: exact matches exist.<br>'
        f'<span class="cellbox orange"></span> treated but <b>no</b> untreated: {nT_un} of {nT_all} treated have no match and are dropped.'),
], height=500, fig_w=60, box="Exact matching")
```

## Exact matching and the curse of dimensionality

```{python}
#| output: asis
rngK = np.random.default_rng(1)
def share_matched(k, n, cats=6, reps=10):
    """Share of treated units with at least one untreated unit in the same cell (k covariates, `cats` groups each)."""
    out = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        Xk = rngK.integers(0, cats, (n, k)); D = rngK.binomial(1, 0.2, n)
        cell = pd.Series([tuple(r) for r in Xk])
        has_c = set(cell[D == 0]); out.append(np.mean([c in has_c for c in cell[D == 1]]))
    return np.mean(out)
KS = np.arange(1, 9)
curve = {n: np.array([share_matched(k, n) for k in KS]) * 100 for n in (1000, 10000)}

s = bse_anim.Steps("curse", figsize=(8.4, 5.0), margins=dict(left=0.12, right=0.97, top=0.95, bottom=0.2))
ax = s.ax
ax.set_xlim(0.6, 8.4); ax.set_ylim(-3, 105)
ax.set_xticks(KS); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{k}\n({6 ** k:,})" for k in KS], fontsize=9.5)
ax.set_xlabel(r"Number of covariates $k$   (number of cells $6^k$)")
ax.set_ylabel("% of treated with an exact match")
s.snap()
for n, col, ypos in ((1000, PURPLE, 0), (10000, T_COL, 1)):
    ax.plot(KS, curve[n], "-o", color=col, lw=2.6, ms=7)
    ax.text(*((2.0, 35) if n == 1000 else (5.6, 80)), f"N = {n:,}", color=col, fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
    s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, "Each covariate is cut into <b>6 groups</b>, as on the previous slide. A cell is one combination of groups, so with k covariates there are 6 × 6 × … × 6 = <b>6<sup>k</sup> cells</b> (in brackets under the axis)."),
    (1, f"Simulation with <b>N = 1,000</b> people (20% treated): with 3 covariates {curve[1000][2]:.0f}% of the treated find an exact match; with 5 only {curve[1000][4]:.0f}%; with 8, {curve[1000][7]:.0f}%."),
    (2, f"<b>N = 10,000</b>: ten times more data only delays the problem ({curve[10000][4]:.0f}% with 5 covariates, {curve[10000][7]:.0f}% with 8). Cells grow ×6 with each covariate, the data do not: the <b>curse of dimensionality</b>."),
], height=500, fig_w=58)
```

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="font-size:0.75em"}
⇒ We need to summarize all of $X$ in **one number**: the propensity score.
:::

# 3 · The propensity score {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## The propensity score

::: {.eq-box-wrap}
::: {.eq-box}
$$p(X) = P(D = 1 \mid X)$$
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
**Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983).** If the CIA holds given $X$, it also holds given the scalar $p(X)$:
:::

$$\big(Y(1), Y(0)\big) \perp\!\!\!\perp D \mid X \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \big(Y(1), Y(0)\big) \perp\!\!\!\perp D \mid p(X)$$

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.82em"}
- Why? $p(X)$ is a **balancing score**: among units with the same $p(X)$, the distribution of $X$ is the same for treated and untreated, $\;D \perp\!\!\!\perp X \mid p(X)$.
- So instead of matching on $k$ covariates, we match on **one** number.
- $p(X)$ is unknown: we **estimate** it, usually with a logit or probit $\;\hat p(X_i) = \Lambda(X_i'\hat\beta)$.
:::

---

## Matching on the propensity score: 2D → 1D → 2D

```{python}
#| output: asis
from matplotlib.patches import ConnectionPatch
rngP2 = np.random.default_rng(57)
nP = 80
toyP = pd.DataFrame({"educ": rngP2.normal(13, 2.4, nP).clip(8, 19), "age": rngP2.normal(40, 10, nP).clip(20, 64)})
toyP["D"] = rngP2.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(-1.0 - 0.45 * (toyP.educ - 13) - 0.06 * (toyP.age - 40)))))
toyP = pd.concat([toyP, pd.DataFrame({"educ": [7.9, 8.4], "age": [21.5, 25.0], "D": [1, 1]})], ignore_index=True)  # 2 extreme treated
nP = len(toyP)
toyP["p"] = smf.logit("D ~ educ + age", toyP).fit(disp=0).predict(toyP)
iT, iC = np.where(toyP.D == 1)[0], np.where(toyP.D == 0)[0]
CAL2 = 0.07
pairsP, droppedP = [], []
for i in iT:                                             # nearest untreated on p-hat, WITH replacement
    j = iC[np.abs(toyP.p.values[iC] - toyP.p[i]).argmin()]
    (pairsP.append((i, j)) if abs(toyP.p[j] - toyP.p[i]) <= CAL2 else droppedP.append(i))
mT = np.array([i for i, _ in pairsP]); mC = np.array([j for _, j in pairsP]); usedP = set(mC)

s = bse_anim.Steps("ps2d", figsize=(8.8, 5.0))
fig = s.fig; s.ax.remove()
ax = fig.add_axes([0.09, 0.12, 0.60, 0.80])
axP = fig.add_axes([0.80, 0.12, 0.09, 0.80])
ax.set_xlim(7.5, 19.5); ax.set_ylim(17, 67); ax.set_xlabel("Education (years)"); ax.set_ylabel("Age")
axP.set_xlim(-1, 1); axP.set_ylim(-0.02, 1.02); axP.grid(False); axP.set_xticks([])
for sp in ("left", "bottom", "top", "right"): axP.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
axP.yaxis.tick_right(); axP.set_yticks([0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]); axP.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
axP.axvline(0, color="black", lw=1.4)
axP.set_title(PHAT + "(X)", fontsize=15, color=PURPLE)
XT, XC = -0.42, 0.42                                     # treated left of the axis, untreated right
axP.text(XT, -0.06, "T", ha="center", color=T_COL, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", clip_on=False)
axP.text(XC, -0.06, "C", ha="center", color=C_COL, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", clip_on=False)
axP.set_visible(False)
scC2 = dots(ax, toyP.educ[iC], toyP.age[iC], C_COL, s=85, label="Untreated")
scT2 = dots(ax, toyP.educ[iT], toyP.age[iT], T_COL, s=85, label="Treated")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=11, frameon=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor=FADE)
s.snap()

def proj(idx, alpha=0.4):
    out = []
    for k in idx:
        xb = XT if toyP.D[k] == 1 else XC
        cp = ConnectionPatch(xyA=(toyP.educ[k], toyP.age[k]), coordsA=ax.transData, xyB=(xb, toyP.p[k]), coordsB=axP.transData,
                             color=T_COL if toyP.D[k] == 1 else C_COL, lw=1.0, alpha=alpha, zorder=1)
        fig.add_artist(cp); out.append(cp)
    return out
# 2-4) project onto the p-hat axis in three batches
axP.set_visible(True)
batches = np.array_split(np.random.default_rng(0).permutation(nP), 3)
pl = []
for b in batches:                                        # cumulative: earlier lines stay
    pl += proj(b, alpha=0.3)
    bT = [k for k in b if toyP.D[k] == 1]; bC = [k for k in b if toyP.D[k] == 0]
    axP.scatter(np.full(len(bT), XT), toyP.p[bT], s=60, color=T_COL, edgecolor="white", lw=1, zorder=3)
    axP.scatter(np.full(len(bC), XC), toyP.p[bC], s=60, color=C_COL, edgecolor="white", lw=1, zorder=3)
    s.snap()
for c_ in pl: c_.remove()
# 5) match on the axis
scC2.set_alpha(0.2); scT2.set_alpha(0.2)
for i, j in pairsP:
    axP.plot([XT, XC], [toyP.p[i], toyP.p[j]], color=PURPLE, lw=1.4, alpha=0.8, zorder=2)
s.snap()
# 6) unused untreated and unmatched treated drop out
axP.scatter(np.full(len(iC), XC), toyP.p[iC], s=60, color=[C_COL if j in usedP else FADE for j in iC],
            edgecolor=["white" if j in usedP else FADE for j in iC], lw=1, zorder=4)
for i in droppedP:
    axP.scatter([XT], [toyP.p[i]], s=120, marker="x", color="#C0392B", lw=2.6, zorder=5)
s.snap()
# 7) back to 2D: only the matched sample
keep = set(mT) | usedP
for sc, idx, col in ((scC2, iC, C_COL), (scT2, iT, T_COL)):
    sc.set_alpha(1); sc.set_facecolor([col if k in keep else FADE for k in idx])
    sc.set_edgecolor(["white" if k in keep else FADE for k in idx])
for i in droppedP:
    ax.scatter(toyP.educ[i], toyP.age[i], s=120, marker="x", color="#C0392B", lw=2.6, zorder=5)
pl = proj(sorted(keep), alpha=0.4)
s.snap()
# 8) matched pairs in 2D
for c_ in pl: c_.remove()
for i, j in pairsP:
    ax.plot([toyP.educ[i], toyP.educ[j]], [toyP.age[i], toyP.age[j]], color=PURPLE, lw=1.1, alpha=0.55, zorder=2)
s.snap()
mean_ = lambda v, idx: toyP[v].values[idx].mean()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, "Two covariates: treated and untreated differ in X."),
    (1, r"Estimate \(\hat p(X)\) with a logit and send every unit to its \(\hat p\): <b>one number</b> per unit (3 clicks)."),
    (4, rf"Match each treated unit to the untreated unit with the closest \(\hat p\) (with replacement, caliper = {CAL2})."),
    (5, f"Unused untreated drop out. The {len(droppedP)} treated with \\(\\hat p\\) far above every untreated have no match within the caliper (×): dropped."),
    (6, "Send the matched units back to the 2D space."),
    (7, f"Pairs share \\(\\hat p\\), <b>not X</b>. But as groups they now look alike: education {mean_('educ', mT):.1f} vs {mean_('educ', mC):.1f} "
        f"(before {mean_('educ', iT):.1f} vs {mean_('educ', iC):.1f}), age {mean_('age', mT):.1f} vs {mean_('age', mC):.1f} "
        f"(before {mean_('age', iT):.1f} vs {mean_('age', iC):.1f})."),
], height=520, fig_w=62, box="Propensity-score matching")
```

::: {.fragment fragment-index=7 style="font-size:0.75em"}
Then estimate the ATT on the matched sample exactly as before: $\;\widehat{\text{ATT}} = \frac{1}{N_1}\sum_{i:\,D_i=1}\big(Y_i - Y_{j(i)}\big)$.
:::

---

## Common support

```{python}
#| output: asis
rngC = np.random.default_rng(8)
nCm = 2500
toyC = pd.DataFrame({"educ": rngC.normal(13, 2.6, nCm).clip(6, 21), "age": rngC.normal(40, 11, nCm).clip(18, 66)})
toyC["D"] = rngC.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(-1.6 - 0.75 * (toyC.educ - 13) - 0.09 * (toyC.age - 40)))))
toyC["p"] = smf.logit("D ~ educ + age", toyC).fit(disp=0).predict(toyC)
rngP = np.random.default_rng(4)
pTc = 0.12 + 0.88 * rngP.beta(2.6, 1.5, 700)            # treated: high scores, none below 0.12
pCc = 0.80 * rngP.beta(1.3, 3.8, 2500)                  # untreated: low scores, none above 0.80
lo_, hi_ = pTc.min(), pCc.max()
bins = np.linspace(0, 1, 41)
hT, _ = np.histogram(pTc, bins); hC, _ = np.histogram(pCc, bins)
s = bse_anim.Steps("support", figsize=(11, 4.2), margins=dict(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.93, bottom=0.14))
ax = s.ax
w = bins[1] - bins[0]
ax.bar(bins[:-1], hT / hT.sum(), width=w, align="edge", color=T_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", label="Treated")
ax.bar(bins[:-1], -hC / hC.sum(), width=w, align="edge", color=C_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", label="Untreated")
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1)
yl = max(hT.max() / hT.sum(), hC.max() / hC.sum()) * 1.15
ax.set_ylim(-yl, yl); ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
tk = np.arange(-0.08, 0.081, 0.04); ax.set_yticks(tk); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{abs(v):.0%}" for v in tk])
ax.set_xlabel(r"$\hat p(X)$"); ax.set_ylabel("Share of the group")
ax.legend(loc="upper left")
s.snap()
ax.axvspan(0, lo_, color=GRAY, alpha=0.2, lw=0); ax.axvspan(hi_, 1, color=GRAY, alpha=0.2, lw=0)
ax.axvline(lo_, color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.6); ax.axvline(hi_, color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.6)
ax.annotate(f"untreated with {PHAT} below\nevery treated: dropped ({(pCc < lo_).sum():,})", xy=(lo_ / 2, -yl * 0.55),
            xytext=(0.2, -yl * 0.8), fontsize=11.5, color=PURPLE, va="center",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=PURPLE, lw=1.2))
ax.text((hi_ + 1) / 2, -yl * 0.45, f"treated with {PHAT}\nabove every\nuntreated: no\ncomparable unit,\ndropped ({(pTc > hi_).sum()})",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11, color=PURPLE)
ax.text((lo_ + hi_) / 2, yl * 0.88, "common support", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=PURPLE, fontweight="bold")
s.snap()
s.show(height=380)
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.75em"}
Stata's `comsup` option keeps only units with $\hat p$ in $[\min \hat p_{D=1},\, \max \hat p_{D=1}]$. Dropping treated units changes **who** the ATT is about: always report how many you lose.
:::

---

## Checking the balancing property: stratify on $\hat p(X)$

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}
`pscore` (Becker & Ichino, 2002) splits $\hat p$ into **blocks** and tests, inside each block, that treated and untreated have the same mean of every $X$: $\;D \perp\!\!\!\perp X \mid p(X)$.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
loC = toyC.p[toyC.D == 1].min()                       # common support: p above the lowest treated
edges = np.array([loC, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1.0])
cs = toyC[toyC.p >= loC].copy()
cs["block"] = np.digitize(cs.p, edges[1:-1])
s = bse_anim.Steps("blocks", figsize=(11.2, 4.3), nrows=2, margins=dict(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.96, bottom=0.1, hspace=0.45))
a1, a2 = s.ax
fcs = ["#F4F4F4", "#FFFFFF"]
for k in range(len(edges) - 1):
    a1.axvspan(edges[k], edges[k + 1], color=fcs[k % 2], zorder=0)
    a1.axvline(edges[k], color=PURPLE, lw=1, alpha=0.6)
    a1.text((edges[k] + edges[k + 1]) / 2, 0.9, f"B{k + 1}", ha="center", fontsize=11.5, color=PURPLE, fontweight="bold",
            transform=a1.get_xaxis_transform())
jit = np.random.default_rng(0)
cT, cC = cs[cs.D == 1], cs[cs.D == 0]
a1.scatter(cT.p, 0.35 + jit.uniform(-0.12, 0.12, len(cT)), s=12, color=T_COL, alpha=0.7, lw=0)
a1.scatter(cC.p, -0.35 + jit.uniform(-0.12, 0.12, len(cC)), s=12, color=C_COL, alpha=0.7, lw=0)
a1.set_xlim(0, 1); a1.set_ylim(-0.6, 0.75); a1.set_yticks([0.35, -0.35]); a1.set_yticklabels(["Treated", "Untreated"])
a1.grid(False); a1.set_xlabel(r"$\hat p(X)$", labelpad=1)
a2.set_visible(False); s.snap()
a2.set_visible(True)
labs = ["All"] + [f"B{k + 1}" for k in range(len(edges) - 1)]
a2.set_xticks(range(len(labs))); a2.set_xticklabels(labs); a2.set_xlim(-0.5, len(labs) - 0.5)
a2.set_ylabel("Mean education")
def mpair(ax, x, g, alpha=1.0):
    mt, mc = g.educ[g.D == 1].mean(), g.educ[g.D == 0].mean()
    ax.plot([x, x], [mt, mc], color=GRAY, lw=1.5, zorder=1, alpha=alpha)
    ax.scatter([x], [mt], s=90, color=T_COL, edgecolor="white", zorder=3, alpha=alpha)
    ax.scatter([x], [mc], s=90, color=C_COL, edgecolor="white", zorder=3, alpha=alpha)
    return stats.ttest_ind(g.educ[g.D == 1], g.educ[g.D == 0], equal_var=False).pvalue
p_all = mpair(a2, 0, toyC)
a2.text(0.25, toyC.educ.mean(), f"p = {p_all:.3f} ✗", fontsize=11, color="#C0392B", va="center", **SYM)
a2.set_ylim(toyC.educ.min() + 3, toyC.educ.max() - 3)
s.snap()
for k in range(len(edges) - 1):
    g = cs[cs.block == k]
    pv = mpair(a2, k + 1, g)
    a2.text(k + 1.12, g.educ.mean(), "✓" if pv > 0.01 else "✗", fontsize=13,
            color="#1E8449" if pv > 0.01 else "#C0392B", va="center", fontweight="bold", **SYM)
s.snap()
s.show(height=385)
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.72em"}
If some $X$ fails in some block, Stata says *"The balancing property is not satisfied — try a different specification"*: add **interactions** or **higher powers** to the logit and run again.
:::

---

## From $\hat p$ to $\hat Y_i(0)$: nearest neighbour, radius or kernel

::: {.fs72}
Once every unit has its $\hat p$, we still have to decide **which controls** stand in for each treated unit, and with **which weights**: $\;\hat Y_i(0) = \sum_j w_{ij}\, Y_j$.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
p0, y0_t = 0.42, 7.0
pc = np.array([0.08, 0.20, 0.30, 0.365, 0.405, 0.475, 0.53, 0.60, 0.72, 0.86])
yc = np.array([12.1, 9.4, 7.8, 6.2, 5.6, 4.8, 6.8, 4.1, 3.6, 2.9])           # earnings of each control (thousand $)
w_nn = (np.abs(pc - p0) == np.abs(pc - p0).min()).astype(float)
r_ = 0.065; w_r = (np.abs(pc - p0) <= r_).astype(float); w_r /= w_r.sum()
h_ = 0.15; u_ = (pc - p0) / h_; w_k = np.where(np.abs(u_) < 1, 0.75 * (1 - u_ ** 2), 0); w_k /= w_k.sum()
s = bse_anim.Steps("nnrk", figsize=(8.6, 5.4), nrows=4, sharex=True,
                   margins=dict(left=0.03, right=0.8, top=0.97, bottom=0.1, hspace=0.35))
labels = ["Data", "Nearest neighbour", f"Radius (r = {r_})", f"Kernel (h = {h_})"]
for k, (ax, lab) in enumerate(zip(s.ax, labels)):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1); ax.set_ylim(-0.55, 1.15); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False); ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1)
    ax.text(0.0, 1.0, lab, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=PURPLE, va="bottom")
    ax.scatter([p0], [0.62], s=150, marker="v", color=T_COL, edgecolor="white", zorder=4)
    ax.plot([p0, p0], [0.5, 0], color=T_COL, lw=1.1, ls=":")
a0 = s.ax[0]
a0.scatter(pc, np.zeros_like(pc), s=90, color=C_COL, edgecolor="white", zorder=3)
for x, y in zip(pc, yc):
    a0.text(x, -0.42, f"{y:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=10, color=C_COL)
a0.text(p0 + 0.02, 0.75, f"treated i: Y = {y0_t:.1f}", fontsize=10.5, color=T_COL)
a0.text(1.02, 0.25, "numbers: Y of\neach control", transform=a0.get_yaxis_transform(), fontsize=10, color=C_COL, va="center")
s.ax[3].set_xlabel(r"$\hat p(X)$  (dot size and small numbers = weight $w_{ij}$)")
for ax in s.ax[1:]: ax.set_visible(False)
s.snap()
for ax, w in zip(s.ax[1:], (w_nn, w_r, w_k)):
    ax.set_visible(True)
    ax.scatter(pc, np.zeros_like(pc), s=30 + 700 * w, color=[C_COL if wi > 0 else FADE for wi in w], edgecolor="white", lw=1.2, zorder=3)
    for j, (x, wi) in enumerate([(x, wi) for x, wi in zip(pc, w) if wi > 0]):
        ax.text(x, -0.32 - 0.22 * (j % 2), f"{wi:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=C_COL)
    yhat = (w * yc).sum()
    ax.text(1.02, 0.3, rf"$\hat Y_i(0)$ = {yhat:.2f}" + "\n" + rf"$\hat\tau_i$ = {y0_t - yhat:+.2f}",
            transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(), fontsize=11, color=PURPLE, va="center")
    if ax is s.ax[2]: ax.axvspan(p0 - r_, p0 + r_, ymin=0.2, ymax=0.5, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.12, lw=0)
    if ax is s.ax[3]:
        xx = np.linspace(p0 - h_, p0 + h_, 100)
        ax.fill_between(xx, 0, 0.75 * (1 - ((xx - p0) / h_) ** 2) * 1.1, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.13, lw=0)
    s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, r"One treated unit \(i\) (▼, \(\hat p = 0.42\)) and ten controls, each with its \(\hat p\) and its \(Y\)."),
    (1, "<b>Nearest neighbour</b>: only the closest control, weight 1 (with k neighbours, 1/k each). What we did so far."),
    (2, "<b>Radius</b>: every control within a distance r of \\(\\hat p_i\\), equal weights. More controls, but you have to choose r."),
    (3, "<b>Kernel</b>: every control, weights falling with the distance (bandwidth h). Uses almost all the data → less variance; no analytical SE ⇒ <b>bootstrap</b>."),
], height=500, fig_w=60, box="Three ways to build Ŷᵢ(0)")
```

# 4 · Back to job training: which matching method wins? {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

## Common support in the NSW data

```{python}
#| output: asis
nsw_o = nsw[nsw["sample"] != 2].copy()
nsw_o[["age", "educ"]] = nsw_o[["age", "educ"]].astype(float)   # int16 would overflow in age**3
nsw_o["agesq"] = nsw_o.age ** 2; nsw_o["agecu"] = nsw_o.age ** 3; nsw_o["educsq"] = nsw_o.educ ** 2
nsw_o["u74"] = (nsw_o.re74 == 0).astype(int); nsw_o["u75"] = (nsw_o.re75 == 0).astype(int)
nsw_o["educ_re74"] = nsw_o.educ * nsw_o.re74
X2 = "age + agesq + agecu + educ + educsq + married + nodegree + black + hisp + re74 + re75 + u74 + u75 + educ_re74"
ps_nsw = smf.logit("treat ~ " + X2, nsw_o).fit(disp=0, method="newton", maxiter=200)
nsw_o["ps"] = ps_nsw.predict(nsw_o).clip(1e-12, 1 - 1e-12)
nsw_o["lo"] = logit_odds(nsw_o.ps)
pmin, pmax = nsw_o.ps[nsw_o.treat == 1].min(), nsw_o.ps[nsw_o.treat == 1].max()
n_off = ((nsw_o.treat == 0) & (nsw_o.ps < pmin)).sum(); n_on = ((nsw_o.treat == 0) & (nsw_o.ps >= pmin)).sum()
bins = np.linspace(-20, 4, 49)
hT, _ = np.histogram(nsw_o.lo[nsw_o.treat == 1], bins); hC, _ = np.histogram(nsw_o.lo[nsw_o.treat == 0], bins)
s = bse_anim.Steps("nsw_support", figsize=(11, 4.1), margins=dict(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.93, bottom=0.17))
ax = s.ax; w = bins[1] - bins[0]
ax.bar(bins[:-1], hT / hT.sum(), width=w, align="edge", color=T_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", label="NSW trainees (185)")
ax.bar(bins[:-1], -hC / hC.sum(), width=w, align="edge", color=C_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", label="CPS adults (15,992)")
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1)
ticks = [1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-3, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9]
ax.set_xticks(logit_odds(np.array(ticks))); ax.set_xticklabels(["1e-8", "1e-6", "0.0001", "0.001", "0.01", "0.1", "0.5", "0.9"])
ax.set_xlim(-20, 4); ax.set_xlabel(r"$\hat p(X)$  (log-odds scale)")
yl = 0.3; ax.set_ylim(-yl, yl); ax.set_yticks([-0.2, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2]); ax.set_yticklabels(["20%", "10%", "0", "10%", "20%"])
ax.set_ylabel("Share of the group"); ax.legend(loc="upper left")
s.snap()
ax.axvspan(-20, logit_odds(pmin), color=GRAY, alpha=0.18, lw=0); ax.axvline(logit_odds(pmin), color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.8)
ax.text(logit_odds(pmin) - 0.3, -0.25, f"{n_off:,} CPS adults with {PHAT} below\nthe lowest trainee ({PHAT} = {pmin:.4f}): dropped", ha="right", fontsize=12, color=PURPLE)
ax.text(logit_odds(pmin) + 0.3, 0.24, f"common support:\n185 trainees, {n_on:,} CPS", ha="left", fontsize=12, color=PURPLE, fontweight="bold")
s.snap()
s.show(height=370)
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.75em"}
Most CPS adults have $\hat p \approx 0$: nobody like them enrolls in the program. They are **useless** as counterfactuals, and matching ignores them.
:::

## Results: the effect of training with five matching methods

```{python}
#| output: asis
mres = pd.read_csv("matching_results.csv")          # exported by TA7.do (psmatch2)
mbal = pd.read_csv("matching_balance.csv")
bias_before = mbal[mbal.method == "Before matching"].bias.abs().mean()
winner = mres.loc[mres.mean_bias.idxmin(), "method"]
rows = [("Naive difference in means", -8498, 582, "185", "15,992", f"{bias_before:.1f}", False),
        ("OLS + X", 1184, 628, "185", "15,992", "–", False)]
rows += [(r.method.replace("pscore", "p̂"), r.att, r.se, f"{r.n_treated:.0f}", f"{r.n_controls:,.0f}", f"{r.mean_bias:.1f}", r.method == winner)
         for r in mres.itertuples()]
body = ""
for k, (m, b, se, nt, nc, mb, win) in enumerate(rows):
    cls = ' class="hl"' if win else (' class="sep"' if k == 2 else "")
    body += (f"<tr{cls}><td>{m}{' 🏆' if win else ''}</td><td>{b:,.0f}</td><td>({se:,.0f})</td>"
             f"<td>{nt}</td><td>{nc}</td><td>{mb}</td></tr>")
html_out(f"""
<table class="baltab restab">
<thead><tr><th>Estimator</th><th>ATT (US$)</th><th>SE</th><th>Participants matched</th><th>Controls used</th><th>Mean |bias| (%)</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>{body}</tbody></table>
""")
```

::: {style="font-size:0.55em; color:#777"}
Outcome: earnings in 1978. All methods on the **common support** (185 participants, 3,856 CPS adults). *Participants matched*: those with a comparable control. *Controls used*: CPS adults with positive weight. *Mean |bias|*: average standardized bias of the 12 covariates after matching. SEs from psmatch2 (they ignore that $\hat p$ is estimated); kernel SE bootstrapped (50 replications).
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
nn = mres[mres.method.str.startswith("NN")]
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment .fs72}}
- Every matching method turns −\\$8,498 into a **positive** effect, between \\${mres.att.min():,.0f} and \\${mres.att.max():,.0f}: the sign flip is robust, the size depends on the method.
- NN uses few controls ({nn.n_controls.min():.0f}–{nn.n_controls.max():.0f}) → larger SEs. Radius and kernel use (almost) all CPS adults on the common support → smaller SEs.
- Which number do we trust? Not the one we like: the one with the **best balance** (next slide).
:::
""")
```

## Which method balances the covariates best?

```{python}
#| output: asis
VARS = ["age", "agesq", "educ", "educsq", "married", "nodegree", "black", "hisp", "re74", "re75", "u74", "u75"]
LABS = ["Age", "Age²", "Education", "Education²", "Married", "No degree", "Black", "Hispanic",
        "Earnings 74", "Earnings 75", "Unemployed 74", "Unemployed 75"]
piv = mbal.assign(ab=mbal.bias.abs()).pivot(index="variable", columns="method", values="ab").reindex(VARS)
order = piv["Before matching"].sort_values().index
yy = np.arange(len(order)); lab = [LABS[VARS.index(v)] for v in order]
MCOL = {"NN on X (Mahalanobis)": PURPLE, "NN on pscore, k = 1": T_COL, "NN on pscore, k = 5": "#E9B44C",
        "Radius (r = 0.01)": C_COL, "Kernel": "#7A9E7E"}
MMK = {"NN on X (Mahalanobis)": "D", "NN on pscore, k = 1": "o", "NN on pscore, k = 5": "o", "Radius (r = 0.01)": "s", "Kernel": "^"}
win_key = winner.replace(" (bootstrap SE)", "")
s = bse_anim.Steps("love", figsize=(9.0, 5.6), ncols=2, sharey=True,
                   margins=dict(left=0.15, right=0.98, top=0.93, bottom=0.24, wspace=0.08))
a1, a2 = s.ax
a1.scatter(piv.loc[order, "Before matching"], yy, marker="^", s=90, color=GRAY, edgecolor="white", zorder=3)
a1.set_yticks(yy); a1.set_yticklabels(lab, fontsize=11); a1.set_xlim(0, 260)
for a_ in (a1, a2):
    a_.grid(False)
    for y_ in yy: a_.axhline(y_, color='#E3E3E3', lw=0.9, zorder=0)
a1.set_title("Before matching", fontsize=13); a1.set_xlabel("|standardized bias| (%)")
a2.set_xlim(0, 32); a2.axvspan(0, 10, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.07, lw=0); a2.axvline(10, color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.2)
a2.set_title("After matching", fontsize=13); a2.set_xlabel("|standardized bias| (%)")
a2.set_visible(False); s.snap()
a2.set_visible(True)
arts = {}
for k, (m, col) in enumerate(MCOL.items()):
    arts[m] = a2.scatter(piv.loc[order, m], yy, marker=MMK[m], s=70, color=col, edgecolor="white", lw=0.8, zorder=3,
                         label=m.replace("pscore", PHAT))
s.fig.legend(handles=list(arts.values()), loc="lower center", ncol=3, fontsize=10, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.56, 0.0))
s.snap()
for m, a in arts.items():
    if m != win_key: a.set_alpha(0.18)
    else: a.set_sizes([110]); a.set_zorder(5)
s.snap()
mb = mres.set_index("method").mean_bias
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, f"<b>Before matching</b>: participants and CPS adults differ by up to {piv['Before matching'].max():.0f}% of a standard deviation (mean {bias_before:.0f}%)."),
    (1, "<b>After matching</b>, every method removes most of the imbalance (note the different scale)."),
    (2, f"🏆 <b>{win_key}</b>: mean |bias| {mb[winner]:.1f}%, largest {piv[win_key].max():.1f}%. "
        f"Worst: {mb.idxmax().replace(' (bootstrap SE)', '').replace('pscore', 'p̂')} ({mb.max():.1f}%)."),
], height=500, fig_w=62, box="Love plot: balance by method")
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment fragment-index=2 .fs72}}
Choose the method by **balance**, decided *before* looking at the ATT, never by the ATT you prefer. Here the winner gives **\\${mres.set_index('method').att[winner]:,.0f}**.
:::
""")
```

## The propensity score before and after matching

```{python}
#| output: asis
mw = pd.read_csv("matching_weights.csv")          # exported by TA7.do: p-hat and matching weights (common support)
T1, C0 = mw.treat == 1, mw.treat == 0
bins = np.linspace(0, 1, 21)
def share(x, w=None):
    h, _ = np.histogram(x, bins, weights=w)
    return h / h.sum()
panels = [("Before matching", None), ("NN on X (Mahalanobis)", "w_mahal"), ("NN on p̂, k = 1", "w_nn1"),
          ("NN on p̂, k = 5", "w_nn5"), ("Radius (r = 0.01)", "w_radius"), ("Kernel", "w_kernel")]
s = bse_anim.Steps("psdist", figsize=(9.6, 5.4), nrows=2, ncols=3, sharex=True, sharey=True,
                   margins=dict(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.92, bottom=0.11, wspace=0.08, hspace=0.32))
w_ = bins[1] - bins[0]
for ax, (ttl, wcol) in zip(s.ax.ravel(), panels):
    if wcol is None:
        ht, hc = share(mw.myscore[T1]), share(mw.myscore[C0])
    else:
        mt, mc = T1 & (mw[wcol] > 0), C0 & (mw[wcol] > 0)
        ht, hc = share(mw.myscore[mt], mw[wcol][mt]), share(mw.myscore[mc], mw[wcol][mc])
    ax.bar(bins[:-1], ht, width=w_, align="edge", color=T_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", lw=0.5)
    ax.bar(bins[:-1], -hc, width=w_, align="edge", color=C_COL, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white", lw=0.5)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8); ax.set_xlim(0, 1); ax.set_ylim(-0.42, 0.42)
    if hc.max() > 0.42:                                   # clipped bar: write its value
        ax.text(bins[1] + 0.02, -0.38, f"{hc.max():.0%} ↓", fontsize=9.5, color=C_COL, va="center")
    ax.set_title(ttl.replace("p̂", PHAT), fontsize=11.5, color=PURPLE if ttl.startswith("NN on X") else "black")
    ax.set_yticks([-0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4]); ax.set_yticklabels(["40%", "20%", "0", "20%", "40%"], fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=9)
    if ttl != "Before matching": ax.set_visible(False)
s.ax[0, 0].text(0.97, 0.3, "participants", ha="right", fontsize=10, color=T_COL, transform=s.ax[0, 0].get_yaxis_transform())
s.ax[0, 0].text(0.97, -0.3, "CPS adults", ha="right", fontsize=10, color=C_COL, transform=s.ax[0, 0].get_yaxis_transform())
for a in s.ax[1]: a.set_xlabel(r"$\hat p(X)$", fontsize=11)
s.snap()
for ax in s.ax.ravel()[1:]: ax.set_visible(True)
s.snap()
anim_steps(s, [
    (0, r"<b>Before matching</b>: \(\hat p\) of the participants (up) and of the CPS adults on the common support (down). Almost all CPS adults sit at \(\hat p < 0.05\)."),
    (1, r"<b>After matching</b>: each CPS adult weighted by how much it is used. The matched CPS distribution now <b>mirrors</b> the participants': the groups are comparable in \(\hat p\)."),
], height=520, fig_w=64, box="How to read it")
```

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 .fs72}
Same check as the love plot, but for $\hat p$. Even matching on $X$ (Mahalanobis), which never uses $\hat p$, balances it. How: each CPS adult enters the histogram with its **matching weight** (how many times, or how much, it is used).
:::

---

## Plot twist: the NSW was an experiment

::: {style="font-size:0.78em"}
The NSW participants were **randomly drawn** from the applicants; the 260 applicants randomized out form an **experimental control group**. So for this program we *know* the answer.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
html_out("""
<div class="groups">
  <div class="grp t"><div class="n">185</div><div class="lab">NSW participants</div><div class="sub">D = 1</div></div>
  <div class="grp ce"><div class="n">260</div><div class="lab">NSW randomized controls</div><div class="sub">the experimental D = 0</div></div>
  <div class="grp cps"><div class="n">15,992</div><div class="lab">CPS adults</div><div class="sub">a survey: non-experimental D = 0</div></div>
</div>
""")
```

::: {.fragment .tight style="font-size:0.66em"}
| Comparison | Effect on 1978 earnings (US$) | SE |
|:---|---:|---:|
| **Experiment**: participants vs randomized controls | **1,794** | (671) |
| Naive: participants vs CPS adults | −8,498 | (582) |
| OLS + X: participants vs CPS adults | 1,184 | (628) |
:::

::: {.fragment .fs75}
**LaLonde (1986)** did exactly what we did today: throw away the experimental controls, use the CPS, and check whether non-experimental methods recover 1,794. Dehejia & Wahba (1999) showed that **matching** gets close.
:::

---

## Did matching recover the experiment?

```{python}
#| output: asis
est = [("Experiment (RCT)", 1794, 671, PURPLE), ("Naive: NSW vs CPS", -8498, 582, GRAY), ("OLS + X", 1184, 628, GRAY)]
est += [((r.method.replace("pscore", PHAT).replace(" (bootstrap SE)", "")) + ("  (best balance)" if r.method == winner else ""), r.att, r.se,
         PURPLE if r.method == winner else T_COL) for r in mres.itertuples()]
s = bse_anim.Steps("summary", figsize=(10.4, 4.4), margins=dict(left=0.33, right=0.97, top=0.95, bottom=0.14))
ax = s.ax
ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(est) - 0.4); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_yticks(range(len(est))); ax.set_yticklabels([e[0] for e in est], fontsize=12)
ax.set_xlim(-10500, 5200); ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel("Effect of training on 1978 earnings (US$), 95% CI")
ax.axvspan(1794 - 1.96 * 671, 1794 + 1.96 * 671, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.08, lw=0)
ax.axvline(1794, color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.4)
def row(k):
    lab, b, se, col = est[k]
    ax.plot([b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se], [k, k], color=col, lw=5, solid_capstyle="round", alpha=0.8)
    ax.scatter([b], [k], s=120, color=col, edgecolor="black", zorder=3)
    ax.text(b + 1.96 * se + 200, k, f"{b:,.0f}", va="center", fontsize=12, color=col)
for k in (0, 1, 2): row(k)
for k in range(3, len(est)): ax.get_yticklabels()[k].set_alpha(0.0)
s.snap()
for k in range(3, len(est)): row(k); ax.get_yticklabels()[k].set_alpha(1)
s.snap()
s.show(height=400)
```

::: {.fragment .fs75}
Once participants are compared with **comparable** CPS adults, every matching estimate lands inside the experimental 95% CI (shaded), the best-balanced one included. **But** we were lucky to observe the right $X$ (past earnings!): without them the CIA fails and no matching method can help (Smith & Todd, 2005).
:::
